trigger: a PR touching server/core/src/rest_api_v1.cpp without docs/user-manual/rest-api.md and without a doc-coupling-exempt line in its body
classification_rationale: not a required doc under the six-item test; the coupling rule `rest-api` demands either a manual edit or an exemption line in the PR body, and the gh pr create hook enforces it
summary: check-docs-drift.py --touch exits non-zero with an empty PR body. Also raised independently by unhappy-path and consistency-auditor in the same wave. Resolution: the PR body carries `doc-coupling-exempt: rest-api — OpenAPI ecosystem enum ordering only; the manual lists the set, which is unchanged`; verified that the check fails without the line and passes with the drafted body.

trigger: reading the anti-vacuous comment in test_json_enum_arrays_equal_vocabulary after the ecosystem requirement became MCP-only
classification_rationale: comment wording only; the code (the MCP_SRC guard) is correct
summary: The comment said every file must carry an ecosystem enum array; OpenAPI arrays are now generated. Resolution: comment reworded in commit 4ac7a6ccf.

trigger: a kEcosystemFamilies row commented out with the declared std::array size unchanged, or a copy-pasted duplicate row
classification_rationale: the table parser claims to derive the live vocabulary but counted a commented-out row and accepted duplicates, so the drift gate could pass while MCP, the manual and the emitters still listed a removed ecosystem
summary: Verified by running the exact regexes on scratch copies (pass with 12 parsed entries for a commented-out row; 11 unique of 12 for a duplicate). unhappy-path reasoned the opposite (false FAIL); the probe outranks the reasoning. Resolution in commit 4ac7a6ccf: `//` comments are stripped before parsing and duplicates raise. Re-proved by the orchestrator with exit codes on scratch copies: real header exit 0 (7 tests OK), commented-out row exit 1 (parsed 11, declared 12), duplicate row exit 1, trailing comment on a live row exit 0.

trigger: openapi_spec_json() regressing from a reference-returning function to one returning a local
classification_rationale: the assertion discriminates only a by-value return, which already fails to compile
summary: Harmless: the check costs one line and its real discrimination is compile-time. Valid but accepted without change (the enum has no accepted-risk value; `rejected` is used for that).

trigger: first call of openapi_spec() per server process: the by-value copy grows past capacity on the first replace
classification_rationale: the Gate 1 summary stated about 398 KB; the retained expanded string is probably 600-800 KB with a ~1.2 MB transient peak (reasoned, not measured). Also noted by unhappy-path (U7).
summary: Negligible against server memory; a shrink_to_fit would only add another 400 KB copy. Valid but accepted without a code change; the PR body states the real retained figure.

trigger: an operator reads docs/user-manual/mcp.md (get_crypto_libraries row) and concludes msi is refused
classification_rationale: pre-existing omission on the MCP surface; the machine-readable schema (mcp_server.cpp:4004) is correct
summary: Untouched by this change. Docs ride in the code PR that owns the surface: it lands with the follow-up that generates the MCP schemas from the table.

trigger: the follow-up reusing the expander for MCP tool schemas, whose ToolDef holds const char* pointers to static literals
classification_rationale: a design constraint for the next change, not a defect here
summary: The MCP catalogue (mcp_server.cpp build_catalogue) needs the expanded strings in static storage; the expander can be hoisted when a second consumer exists. Recorded for the MCP follow-up; nothing wrong in this change.

trigger: token typo or deletion; unescaped or empty table; @@ in a name; a new route with a hand-typed ecosystem array; the spec chain wrapped in a function; load-induced gateway docs-test timeout
classification_rationale: each scenario is already caught by the C++ pin case, the Python count/regex guard or check-api-parity.py in CI; the hand-typed-array and lambda-wrap gaps existed before this change
summary: Nine-entry register (U1-U9), none introduced and none blocking. Valid but accepted: each is already guarded as described, so no change was warranted.

Resolution restated against the final branch: the drafted PR body (not yet raised) carries `doc-coupling-exempt: rest-api — OpenAPI ecosystem enum ordering only; docs/user-manual/inventory.md lists the set, which is unchanged` as a visible line; `check-docs-drift.py --touch origin/dev HEAD` exits 1 without it and 0 with it. The rule's own doc is rest-api.md; the table of ecosystems is in inventory.md.
classification_rationale: the original `absence` label was wrong: rest-api.md is not a required doc for an ordering-only change, so nothing required is missing; the finding is that the coupling rule needs a stated exemption, which is process wording in the PR body

summary: Final state: parse_ecosystem_table strips both `//` and `/* */` comments, requires the parsed count to equal the declared std::array size and rejects duplicates; software_catalog_rules.hpp also fails to compile on a block-commented row, a duplicate, an empty table or a name outside the renderers' charset (consteval check under static_assert); the vocabulary test has 19 cases covering each form.

Superseded by the single-static redesign (commit 3d6ab2885): openapi_spec() is one function-local static, built by expand_ecosystem_tokens with one reserve at the largest size the string reaches and in-place replaces, so there is no second copy and no growth reallocation; the served document is about 397 KB (397,336 bytes measured) and openapi_spec_json()'s capacity-minus-size is asserted below 4096. The original sre estimate of 600-800 KB with a 1.2 MB transient described the removed two-static shape.
classification_rationale: the Gate 1 figure of about 398 KB was right for the retained string once the by-value copy and the second static were removed; the original finding described the superseded design

summary: Unchanged disposition; the schema anchor has moved with the dev merge: the get_crypto_libraries ecosystem enum is at mcp_server.cpp:4006 (was :4004). Lands with M.10b.

Final state: the hand-typed-array and wrapped-chain gaps are now closed by tests, not accepted. The vocabulary gate walks the decoded unexpanded document and fails any ecosystem enum that is not a generator token (and counts every token against the ecosystem sites), and check-api-parity.py raises named AnchorErrors for a wrapped chain, a second static or any extra statement. The remaining items (token typo on a new route, table-name hygiene) fail the C++ sweep or the compile-time charset check before merge.
